name: Scandinavian Defense
description: A direct Black repertoire against e4 that teaches immediate central counterplay and simple development after White reacts.

branches.title: Main Line: Challenge e4
branches.description: Learn the default Scandinavian idea against 1.e4.

moves.title: White claims center
moves.explanation: White controls d5 and f5. Black should challenge this center immediately. e4 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. In the Scandinavian, Black accepts queen activity early but must avoid moving it too many times; White develops with tempo.

moves.title: Strike with d5
moves.explanation: d5 attacks e4 at once. This is the core Scandinavian idea: meet the center before it grows. d5 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. In the Scandinavian, Black accepts queen activity early but must avoid moving it too many times; White develops with tempo.

moves.title: Trade or capture on d5
moves.explanation: exd5 shows how trades enter the opening. This is an equal trade. Equal trades are good when they improve your structure, open a file, or remove an active enemy piece. After a trade, ask which file opened and which piece should improve next.

moves.title: Trade or capture on d5
moves.explanation: Qxd5 shows how trades enter the opening. This capture should only be played because it gains time, opens lines, or solves a concrete problem. After a trade, ask which file opened and which piece should improve next.

moves.title: Develop to c3
moves.explanation: Nc3 develops a knight to c3. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.title: Connect the pieces
moves.explanation: Qa5 is a calm queen move after development has started. The queen should support pieces and connect rooks, not run out early and get chased.

branches.title: Recapture Carefully
branches.description: If White takes on d5, recapture and expect to lose a tempo to Nc3.

moves.title: White starts
moves.explanation: White takes central space. e4 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. moves.title: Challenge
moves.explanation: Attack e4. d5 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. In the Scandinavian, Black accepts queen activity early but must avoid moving it too many times; White develops with tempo.

moves.title: White captures
moves.explanation: White removes the d5 pawn and opens the queen file. exd5 shows how trades enter the opening. This is an equal trade. Equal trades are good when they improve your structure, open a file, or remove an active enemy piece. After a trade, ask which file opened and which piece should improve next.

moves.title: Recommended: recapture
moves.explanation: Qxd5 restores material. The beginner lesson is to recapture, then accept that the queen may move again after Nc3. Qxd5 shows how trades enter the opening. This capture should only be played because it gains time, opens lines, or solves a concrete problem. After a trade, ask which file opened and which piece should improve next.

ideas: If White captures, recapture and develop.
Avoid moving the queen repeatedly without purpose.
In the Scandinavian, Black accepts queen activity early but must avoid moving it too many times; White develops with tempo.
Trade only when it improves your position, removes danger, or opens a useful file.
By move 8-12, you should know your early middlegame plan: safe king, active pieces, and one central break.
commonMistakes: Playing for tricks instead of central clarity.
Stopping after memorized moves and playing without a plan.
Trading automatically without asking what improves afterward.
Starting an attack before castling or finishing development.
